brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: There are bases on two storeys with a book row (prop:1) on top of the upper base (cover:0,0,1;full;top). Only that one cover takes books: the configurator refused books on the lower half-base covers because the upper base is in the way.
The configurator checks fit and collisions only. It doesn't model strength or load, and how strong the parts are depends on the material and print settings you choose. I can't claim any load rating.
drawer:0#0,-1#cut and drawer:0#-1,0#cut sit in the cut faces of the two half bases.

finish.summary: I built a small two-storey shelf unit with two drawers, and the checks pass with no clashes. I can't give it a 50 kg rating, because the configurator only checks that parts fit and don't collide. It doesn't model strength or load. There are 38 parts: a full base at the bottom, two half bases beside it, and a full base stacked on the middle one. The two drawers sit in the cut faces of the half bases. All open faces are closed with end caps, the joints are bolted, and there are top covers on the upper base and both half bases. I put a row of books on the top cover. Books won't fit on the lower half-base covers because the upper base gets in the way, so the unit holds one row of books plus whatever goes in the drawers. You can't stack a base on the half bases, so the top shelf is only one cell wide.

M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
